subject: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log

Team — attaching the April dashboard and a short action log for QBR prep. High-level context before you dig in:

- Why this matters: ACME’s usage spike last quarter exposed some large tail-latency regressions on our hosted API; engineering took mitigations but we need to present: what happened, what we fixed, and commitments for QBR.
- Focus areas for the exec readout: latency (p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens, 30/90-day uptime trends, active customer usage (DAU/MAU for ACME account), and inferred cost drivers (batching miss rate, cold-starts).

Key asks (owners & ETA in the attached PDF):
- Jonas: Provide final p95/p99 graphs with annotation of the incident window and the exact kernel fallback timestamps (ETA: 24 hours).
- Laura: Update the cost breakdown slide to show per-customer incremental unit economics (ACME highlight) and call out the projected benefit from caching profile changes (ETA: tomorrow noon).
- Vivek: Confirm uptime SLA calc (including recent maintenance windows) and prepare a 1-slide incident summary for the QBR deck (ETA: 48 hours).
- Markus: Validate the proposed fallback policy in the doc; note any customer-impact risk (ETA: 48 hours).

I’ve cc’d Sarah from ACME so they have visibility; we will not share internal kernel-level notes with external stakeholders — Sarah, expect a customer-facing summary next week, not raw logs.

Attachments: 2027-04-kpi-dashboard-v3.pdf, qbr-deck-draft-ACME.pptx

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log

Irene — getting started on the latency visuals. Quick notes from my first pass:

- p95 looks stable after 2027-04-05 mitigation; p99 shows two spikes: 2027-03-28 03:12 UTC and 2027-04-02 06:45 UTC. Both align with a kernel fallback we triggered for that model family.
- I’ll add vertical annotations with fallback reason (memory pressure / kernel mismatch) and the duration of the degraded tail.
- ETA: will push the updated PNGs to the Drive link by 2027-04-22T09:00-07:00.

Question for Vivek: do we want the uptime slide to exclude the 30-minute scheduled maintenance on 2027-03-30? I can generate both numbers but want clarity for the QBR narrative.

— Jonas
Senior Director, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log

Thanks — I updated slide 4 in the deck (cost breakdown). Highlights:

- Observed 18% increase in cost per 1M tokens for ACME year-over-year when their large-context workflows were enabled.
- Primary drivers: 1) increased average context length (40% longer), 2) batching miss rate up from 12% to 21% (more single-shot calls).
- Projection: enabling prefix caching and a small batching incentive could reduce incremental cost by ~9% over next quarter.

Actionable ask: Sarah — would ACME be open to a short implementation window to enable prefix caching for a subset of their workflows? We’d like to trial for 2 weeks and report cost impact at the next check-in.

ETA to finalize the cost chart: 2027-04-22T13:00-07:00.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log

Irene — agree with excluding scheduled maintenance from the uptime calc for the customer-facing SLA figure; include both numbers in the appendix. Notes:

- Uptime: 99.92% excluding scheduled maintenance for the quarter; including maintenance it’s 99.88%.
- Incident summary: the March p99 spike was caused by a sudden increase in long-context unlocks causing a higher-than-expected KV cache eviction rate. The mitigation rolled on 2027-04-05 reduced the eviction rate by ~60%.
- I’ll draft the 1-slide incident summary and add a short timeline and owner list (SRE on-call, Runtime, Customer Success). ETA: 2027-04-23T10:00-07:00.

Also, Markus — please confirm whether the proposed fallback policy has tolerable customer impact; if it does, we’ll codify it as the default for the dedicated tier.

— Vivek
VP, Reliability Engineering
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KPI orchestration: April dashboard, QBR prep, and owner action log

Quick readout and risks from my side:

- Fallback policy: lower-cost model variant fallback is acceptable for non-critical read-only workloads (batch inference) but not for transactional low-latency calls. I flagged customer-impact risk on slide 7.
- My recommended mitigation for the QBR: propose a two-tier fallback matrix (Dedicated: no model fallback for SLA routes; Hosted: fallback allowed with opt-out). This reduces immediate operational risk and gives sales a clear position.
- I validated the timeline on the incident slide — runtime annotations look accurate.

Irene — assembling a one-page exec summary now; I’ll attach it to the deck in Drive and push final copies by 2027-04-24T09:00-07:00.

— Markus
Head of Product Reliability
Redwood Inference
